THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  67

President of the Southeastern State Normal School at Durant, Oklahoma. He was a member of the Society of Friends.

Mr. Will I. Hunt, who was Professor of Greek and Mental Science at the administration of 1887, later received the College, and by the spring of 1887 had earned the A.B. degree. He left the faculty after a year.

Mr. E. R. Glover, who was with the College 1886-1887, served for many years as County Clerk of Stephens County, Texas, and at the time of writing this thesis he was still as the County Surveyor.

Mr. Alexander C. Brown, who was teacher of ancient languages, logic, and rhetoric for the last two years of the College's session, had come to the faculty with more of a background of college-teaching experience than any of the other faculty members. In the year 1876, he had been the colleague of such Professors as Halbell and Holland. At the age of seventeen he had entered the University of Virginia at Portsmouth. After two years of study there he had spent two years in passing examinations at Emory and Henry College, graduated in 1869, and later spent some years as missionary in China.

Concerning Mr. B. J. Hunt, the information is vague. For the last two years (1888-1890) he seems to have been responsible for some of the preparatory work and was regarded as an effective teacher. It appears the writer has seen no bachelor some thirty-five years old and with no family connections.
